qa.q: Meena lives with her mother, father and little brother. What kind of family is this?
qa.e: Parents and their children living together make a small family.

qa.q: Who is your mother's brother?
qa.e: Your mother's brother is your mama. Your father's younger brother is your chacha.

qa.q: Who is your father's mother?
qa.e: Your father's mother is your dadi. Your mother's mother is your nani.

qa.q: In a joint family, who usually lives together?
qa.a: Grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts and cousins
qa.e: A joint family has many relatives from different generations living in one home.

qa.q: Aman lives with his nani and nana. Is this a real family?
qa.a: Yes, people who live together and care for each other are a family
qa.e: Families come in many shapes. Love and care make a family, not its size.

qa.q: Your bua is your father's ___.
qa.e: Bua is the name for your father's sister.

qa.q: Which of these is a good thing about living in a joint family?
qa.a: There are many people to share work and stories with
qa.e: In a joint family, many hands share the work, and children get to hear stories from grandparents.

qa.q: Two new babies are born in Pooja's small family of 3. How many people are in her family now?
qa.e: There were 3 people. 2 babies joined. 3 + 2 = 5.

qa.q: Dadi finds it hard to climb stairs. How can you help?
qa.a: Hold her hand and go up slowly with her
qa.e: Walking slowly beside her and giving a hand keeps her safe.

qa.q: Nana wants to talk about his childhood. What should Ravi do?
qa.e: Listening shows love and respect. Elders' stories also teach us about the past.

qa.q: Why might elders need help with small things?
qa.a: As people grow old, their bodies can become weaker
qa.e: Old age can make eyes, knees and memory weaker, so small tasks may become hard.

qa.q: Which of these shows respect for elders?
qa.e: Greeting elders politely, like saying namaste, shows respect.

qa.q: Nani often forgets to drink water. What is a caring idea?
qa.a: Remind her gently and bring her a glass of water
qa.e: A gentle reminder helps her stay healthy without hurting her feelings.

qa.q: What can grandparents teach us?
qa.a: Old stories, songs and family recipes
qa.e: Elders have lived a long life and know many stories, songs and recipes.

qa.q: Dadu lives in another city. How can Sana stay close to him?
qa.a: Call him and tell him about her day
qa.e: Phone calls, letters and visits keep us close to elders who live far away.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT a kind way to help an elder?
qa.a: Taking away their walking stick for fun
qa.e: A walking stick helps elders balance. Taking it away could make them fall.

qa.q: Arjun and Imran both want the swing. What should they do?
qa.e: Taking turns is fair. Both friends get to enjoy the swing.

qa.q: You broke your friend's pencil by mistake. What should you say?
qa.e: Saying sorry shows you care about your friend's feelings.

qa.q: Which of these is a good friend?
qa.a: Someone who helps you when you are sad
qa.e: A good friend is kind and helps you when you need it.

qa.q: A new boy who speaks Tamil joins your class. You speak Hindi. Can you be friends?
qa.a: Yes, friends can speak different languages
qa.e: Friendship is about kindness. You can even teach each other words in your languages!

qa.q: Your friend wins the drawing contest. What is a friendly thing to do?
qa.e: Good friends are happy for each other's success.

qa.q: Your friend forgot his tiffin. What can you do?
qa.a: Share some of your food with him
qa.e: Sharing food when a friend has none is a caring thing to do.

qa.q: Your friend shares a secret about a surprise party. What should you do?
qa.a: Keep the surprise until the party
qa.e: Friends trust each other. Keeping a happy surprise secret shows you are trustworthy.

qa.q: Riya has 6 toffees. She shares them equally with her friend Neha. How many toffees does each girl get?
qa.e: 6 toffees shared equally between 2 girls is 3 each.

qa.q: What is a mela?
qa.a: A big fair where people shop, eat and enjoy rides
qa.e: A mela is a fair. People gather there to shop, eat, watch shows and enjoy rides.

qa.q: Which of these would you most likely ride at a mela?
qa.e: Merry-go-rounds and giant wheels are common mela rides.

qa.q: The Pushkar fair is held in which state?
qa.e: The Pushkar fair is held in Pushkar, a town in Rajasthan.

qa.q: Which animal is the Pushkar fair famous for?
qa.e: Many camels are brought to the Pushkar fair to be decorated, shown and traded.

qa.q: Why do many melas happen after harvest time?
qa.a: Farmers have finished their work and have crops to sell and celebrate
qa.e: After the harvest, farmers have time and something to celebrate, so many melas happen then.

qa.q: Ravi has ₹40. A toy costs ₹25. How much money will he have left?
At a mela, a person makes puppets dance with strings. What is this show called?
qa.e: Puppets moved by strings, called kathputli, are a famous folk art of Rajasthan.

qa.q: Which of these is a snack you might find at a mela?
qa.e: Jalebi is a sweet snack fried fresh at many melas.

qa.q: Who makes clay pots and diyas?
qa.e: A potter shapes wet clay, often on a spinning wheel, and then bakes it to make it hard.

qa.q: Why should we respect every worker at the mela?
qa.a: Every kind of work is useful and needs effort
qa.e: From the sweeper to the cook, every worker helps the mela run well.

qa.q: Who runs the giant wheel?
qa.e: A ride operator starts, stops and looks after the ride so people stay safe.

qa.q: A woman draws pretty patterns on people's hands with henna. She is a ___.
qa.e: Mehendi artists draw designs with henna paste, which leaves an orange-brown colour.

qa.q: After the mela ends, who cleans up the ground?
qa.e: Cleaners pick up litter so the ground is clean again. We can help by using dustbins.

qa.q: Which of these is the best way to treat a stall owner?
qa.a: Speak politely and say thank you
qa.e: Being polite and paying for what we take shows respect for their work.

qa.q: A man makes a show where puppets dance on strings. Which state is this kathputli art famous in?
qa.e: Kathputli string puppets are a famous folk art of Rajasthan.

qa.q: Which worker would you need to fix a torn chappal at the mela?
qa.e: A cobbler repairs shoes and chappals.

qa.q: What should you do in a big crowd at the mela?
qa.e: Holding hands keeps you close to your family in a crowd.

qa.q: A stranger says, 'Come with me, I will buy you a toy.' What should you do?
qa.a: Say no and go to your grown-up
qa.e: Never go with a stranger. Say no and tell a trusted adult at once.

qa.q: Which information should you know by heart?
qa.a: Your name and your parent's phone number
qa.e: If you are lost, helpers can contact your family with your parent's name and phone number.

qa.q: Who is a safe person to ask for help if you are lost at a mela?
qa.a: A police officer or the help desk
qa.e: Police officers and help desk staff are there to help lost children.

qa.q: What is the emergency helpline number in India that works across the country?
qa.e: 112 is India's single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance help.

qa.q: Why should a family fix a meeting place before entering the mela?
qa.a: So everyone knows where to go if they get separated
qa.e: A meeting place like the main gate helps a lost person find the family quickly.

qa.q: Why should we not push in a crowd?
qa.a: People may fall and get hurt
qa.e: Pushing can make people fall. Walking calmly keeps everyone safe.

qa.q: You are lost and scared. What is the FIRST thing to do?
qa.e: Staying calm helps you think and find a helper. Running away makes it harder for your family to find you.

qa.q: Which festival is called the festival of lights?
qa.e: On Diwali, people light diyas and lamps in and around their homes.

qa.q: Which festival is known as the festival of colours?
qa.e: On Holi, people play with colours and coloured water.

qa.q: On which date do we celebrate Christmas?
qa.e: Christmas is celebrated every year on 25 December.

qa.q: Onam is a harvest festival of which state?
qa.e: Onam is Kerala's harvest festival, with flower pookalams and a big feast.

qa.q: Bihu is a festival of which state?
qa.e: Bihu is celebrated in Assam with music and the lively Bihu dance.

qa.q: Which of these is a national festival celebrated by all Indians?
qa.e: Independence Day, on 15 August, is celebrated all over India by everyone.

qa.q: Eid ul-Fitr is celebrated at the end of which month?
qa.e: Eid ul-Fitr comes at the end of Ramzan, the month of fasting.

qa.q: Why are Pongal, Bihu and Baisakhi called harvest festivals?
qa.a: They are celebrated when crops are ready and gathered
qa.e: These festivals celebrate the crops being gathered and thank nature for food.

qa.q: Which sweet is offered during Ganesh Chaturthi?
qa.e: Modak, a sweet dumpling with coconut and jaggery, is linked with Ganesh Chaturthi.

qa.q: What do people fly on Makar Sankranti?
qa.e: Flying kites is a big Makar Sankranti custom, especially in Gujarat and Rajasthan.

qa.q: Til-gur sweets are made from sesame and ___.
qa.e: Til means sesame and gur means jaggery. They are mixed to make sweets for Makar Sankranti.

qa.q: On what is the Onam sadya served?
qa.e: The Onam feast is served on a banana leaf, a custom from Kerala.

qa.q: What is a langar?
qa.a: Free food served to everyone at a gurdwara
qa.e: At the langar, everyone sits together and eats the same food, no matter who they are.

qa.q: Colourful patterns drawn at the doorstep with rice flour or coloured powder are called ___.
qa.e: Rangoli and kolam are floor patterns that welcome guests during festivals.

qa.q: Which item is used to decorate homes at Christmas?
qa.a: A decorated Christmas tree with a star
qa.e: Families decorate a Christmas tree with lights, bells and a star on top.

qa.q: Gujiya is a sweet many families make for which festival?
qa.e: Gujiya, a sweet stuffed pastry, is popular at Holi in north India.

qa.q: Why do people say festivals bring us together?
qa.a: Families, friends and neighbours celebrate and share joy
qa.e: Festivals are times to meet, share food and enjoy together.

qa.q: Your friend Harpreet celebrates Gurpurab. What is a friendly thing to do?
qa.e: Wishing friends on their festivals shows respect and friendship.

qa.q: Why should we avoid very loud crackers?
qa.a: They scare animals and disturb babies and elders
qa.e: Loud bangs frighten animals and can trouble babies, elders and sick people. Smoke also dirties the air.

qa.q: Which is a nature-friendly way to play Holi?
qa.a: Use colours made from flowers and turmeric
qa.e: Natural colours from flowers, leaves and turmeric are gentler on skin and nature.

qa.q: On Independence Day, schools hoist the national flag. Who celebrates this day?
qa.e: Independence Day is a national festival for every Indian, everywhere.

qa.q: What do people often say to each other on Eid?
qa.e: 'Eid Mubarak' means 'blessed Eid'. People hug and greet each other with these words.

qa.q: After the colony Diwali party, the park is full of wrappers. What should the children do?
qa.a: Help clean up and put waste in dustbins
qa.e: Celebrating together also means cleaning up together.

qa.q: Which of these shows togetherness during a festival?
qa.e: Sharing food with neighbours brings people closer.

qa.q: Which part of a plant holds it firmly in the soil?
qa.e: Roots spread in the soil and hold the plant in place, like an anchor.

qa.q: Which part carries water from the roots to the leaves?
qa.e: The stem works like a pipe that carries water up to the leaves.

qa.q: Which part of a plant makes food for it?
qa.e: Leaves use sunlight, air and water to make food for the plant.

qa.q: A carrot is which part of the plant?
qa.e: The orange part of a carrot grows under the soil. It is a root that stores food.

qa.q: Which of these is a tall tree?
qa.e: Neem grows into a big tree with a thick, hard trunk. The others are small plants.

qa.q: Which plant is a shrub — bushy, with many woody stems, but not as tall as a tree?
qa.e: A rose plant is a shrub. Mango, peepal and coconut are tall trees.

qa.q: The thick, hard stem of a tree is called the ___.
qa.e: A tree's main stem is called its trunk. It is hard and woody.

qa.q: Most plants need which of these to grow well?
qa.e: Plants need sunlight, water and air to make food and stay healthy.

qa.q: Which part do we eat in spinach (palak)?
qa.e: We cook and eat the green leaves of the spinach plant.

qa.q: Which part of the cauliflower plant do we eat?
qa.e: The white part of a cauliflower is a tight bunch of flower buds.

qa.q: The thin lines you see on a leaf are called ___.
qa.e: Veins are thin lines that carry water to all parts of the leaf.

qa.q: Why do bees visit flowers?
qa.e: Bees drink nectar from flowers and use it to make honey.

qa.q: Which flower grows in ponds and is India's national flower?
qa.e: The lotus grows in water and is the national flower of India.

qa.q: Which of these is the colourful part of a flower?
qa.e: Petals are the soft, colourful parts of a flower.

qa.q: Which plant has very big leaves that are used as plates in South India?
qa.e: Banana leaves are large and strong, so food is served on them.

qa.q: After a flower is visited by bees, what does it often grow into?
qa.e: Many flowers turn into fruits, and the fruits hold seeds.

qa.q: What does a seed need to start growing?
qa.e: Seeds need water, air and warmth to sprout.

qa.q: When a seed sprouts, which part usually comes out first?
qa.e: The root comes out first so the young plant can hold on and take in water.

qa.q: How do cotton seeds travel to new places?
qa.a: They are blown by the wind
qa.e: Cotton seeds have soft fluffy hairs that help the wind carry them.

qa.q: How can a coconut travel far away?
qa.e: A coconut has a light, hairy covering that helps it float on sea water.

qa.q: Which fruit has only ONE big seed?
qa.e: A mango has one big seed in the middle. The others have many seeds.

qa.q: Which of these is a seed that we eat?
qa.e: Rice grains are seeds. We also eat wheat, dal and peas, which are seeds.

qa.q: Rahul planted 4 seeds in each of his 3 pots. How many seeds did he plant in all?
qa.e: 3 pots with 4 seeds in each is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 seeds.

qa.q: Why do seeds need to travel away from the parent plant?
qa.a: So the new plants get enough space, water and light
qa.e: If all seeds fell under the parent plant, they would be crowded and get less light and water.

qa.q: What does a cow eat?
qa.e: A cow is a plant-eater. It eats grass, leaves and fodder.

qa.q: Where do many birds build their nests?
qa.e: Trees give birds a safe, high place to build nests.

qa.q: What do bees drink from flowers?
qa.e: Nectar is a sweet juice in flowers. Bees use it to make honey.

qa.q: Lions in the Gir forest of Gujarat eat deer. Deer eat grass. If all the grass dried up, what would happen to the lions?
qa.a: They would have less food, because the deer would go hungry too
qa.e: Lions depend on plants through the animals they eat. Less grass means fewer deer for the lions.

qa.q: Which animal eats mainly plants?
qa.e: Goats eat grass, leaves and plant parts. The others eat other animals.

qa.q: Which of these do people get from plants?
qa.e: Cotton comes from the cotton plant. Glass, iron and plastic do not come from plants.

qa.q: Monkeys live in trees. What else do trees give them?
qa.e: Monkeys eat fruits, leaves and flowers from trees.

qa.q: In the food chain 'grass → rabbit → fox', which one makes its own food?
qa.e: Plants like grass make their own food using sunlight. Animals cannot make their own food.

qa.q: What do bees carry from one flower to another?
qa.e: Pollen is a fine yellow powder. Carrying it between flowers helps them make seeds.

qa.q: How do birds help plants?
qa.a: They drop seeds in new places
qa.e: Birds eat fruits and later drop the seeds far from the parent tree.

qa.q: How do earthworms help plants?
qa.a: They make the soil soft and airy
qa.e: Earthworms tunnel through soil, letting air and water reach the roots.

qa.q: Why do farmers use cow dung manure in their fields?
qa.a: It makes the soil rich for plants
qa.e: Manure adds nutrients to the soil, so crops grow well.

qa.q: Seeds with tiny hooks travel by ___.
qa.a: Sticking to animal fur and clothes
qa.e: Hooks help seeds hold on to fur or clothes, so animals carry them to new places.

qa.q: Why is it good for flowers when butterflies visit them?
qa.a: Butterflies carry pollen, which helps flowers make seeds
qa.e: Like bees, butterflies carry pollen from flower to flower.

qa.q: Plants and animals helping each other is like a ___.
qa.e: Plants give food and shelter; animals help spread pollen and seeds. Both gain.

qa.q: Which of these is an animal helping a plant?
qa.a: A bee visiting a mustard flower
qa.e: The bee carries pollen and helps the mustard flower make seeds. In the others, the plant helps the animal.

qa.q: What is a habitat?
qa.a: The natural home of a plant or animal
qa.e: A habitat is where a living thing lives and finds food, water and shelter.

qa.q: Which animal is best suited to life in the desert?
qa.e: Camels can walk on hot sand and go many days without drinking water.

qa.q: What is inside a camel's hump?
qa.e: A camel's hump stores fat, which the body can use for energy when food is scarce.

qa.q: How does a fish breathe in water?
qa.e: Fish have gills that take in the air dissolved in water.

qa.q: Which animal lives in the cold mountains of Ladakh and has thick, long hair?
qa.e: The yak's thick, long hair keeps it warm in the freezing cold.

qa.q: Why does a cactus have a thick, fleshy stem?
qa.a: To store water in the dry desert
qa.e: Deserts get very little rain, so the cactus stores water in its stem.

qa.q: A frog can live both in water and on land. Which of these is also true for a frog?
qa.e: Frogs lay their eggs in water, and the tadpoles grow there before living on land too.

qa.q: Which plant grows in ponds?
qa.e: The lotus grows in ponds, with its leaves and flowers floating above the water.

qa.q: It is a very hot day. What can you do for the birds?
qa.a: Keep a bowl of clean water on the balcony
qa.e: In hot weather, birds find it hard to get water. A bowl of water helps them.

qa.q: Your friend is pulling a cat's tail. What should you say?
qa.a: Please stop, it hurts the cat
qa.e: Animals feel pain. We should be gentle with them.

qa.q: Why should we not pluck flowers for no reason?
qa.a: Flowers are part of the plant and become fruits and seeds
qa.e: Flowers help plants make fruits and seeds. They also feed bees and butterflies.

qa.q: Which is India's national bird?
qa.e: The peacock (Indian peafowl) is India's national bird.

qa.q: Which is India's national animal?
qa.e: The tiger is India's national animal. The elephant is the national heritage animal.

qa.q: Which is India's national tree?
qa.e: The banyan is India's national tree. Its branches grow roots that hang down to the ground.

qa.q: A spider has made a web in a corner of the garden. Is the spider useful?
qa.a: Yes, it catches flies and mosquitoes
qa.e: Spiders catch insects like flies and mosquitoes in their webs.

qa.q: You see an injured bird on the road. What is the best thing to do?
qa.a: Tell an adult, who can contact an animal helper or vet
qa.e: An adult can safely help the bird and call someone who treats animals.

qa.q: Which of these helps protect nature?
qa.e: Planting saplings adds trees that give shade, fruits and homes for birds.

qa.q: What did people do in the Chipko movement?
qa.a: Hugged trees to save them from being cut
qa.e: Villagers in the Uttarakhand hills held on to trees so they could not be cut.

qa.q: The Bishnoi people of Rajasthan are known for protecting which animal?
qa.e: Bishnoi communities protect blackbucks and khejri trees in the desert.

qa.q: On which date is World Environment Day celebrated?
qa.e: World Environment Day is on 5 June every year.

qa.q: Why are forests important for animals?
qa.a: They give animals food and homes
qa.e: Forests are habitats where animals find food, water and shelter.

qa.q: Which habit helps keep a river clean?
qa.e: Garbage, paint and plastic make river water dirty and harm fish and other living things.

qa.q: Van Mahotsav is held in the first week of which month?
qa.e: Van Mahotsav, a week of planting trees, is held in the first week of July, when the rains begin in much of India.

qa.q: Each of 4 children plants 2 saplings on Van Mahotsav. How many saplings are planted in all?
qa.e: 4 children planting 2 each is 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 saplings.

qa.q: What is the main source of fresh water on Earth?
qa.e: Rain fills rivers, lakes, ponds and wells, and soaks into the ground.

qa.q: Why can we not drink sea water?
qa.e: Sea water has a lot of salt. Drinking it is harmful.

qa.q: Where does the river Ganga begin?
qa.e: The Ganga starts from the Gangotri glacier in the Himalayas in Uttarakhand.

qa.q: Water found under the ground is called ___.
qa.e: Rainwater soaks into the soil and is stored under the ground as groundwater.

qa.q: Which of these takes water out from under the ground?
qa.e: Hand pumps and borewells pull up groundwater.

qa.q: What is a stepwell?
qa.a: An old well with steps going down to the water
qa.e: Stepwells have steps that lead down to the water. They were built to store water in dry areas.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT a source of fresh water?
qa.e: The sea has salty water. Rivers, lakes and rain give fresh water.

qa.q: Snow on mountains melts in summer. Where does this water go?
qa.e: Melting snow flows down as streams that join rivers.

qa.q: Which of these needs water?
qa.e: Rice is cooked in boiling water.

qa.q: Why do farmers need water?
qa.e: Crops need water to grow. Farmers get it from rain, rivers, wells and canals.

qa.q: Which crop is usually grown in fields filled with water?
qa.e: Rice is often grown in fields covered with standing water.

qa.q: How can we make drinking water safe?
qa.e: Boiling kills germs and a filter removes dirt and germs.

qa.q: What can happen if we drink dirty water?
qa.e: Dirty water can have germs that cause illnesses like diarrhoea.

qa.q: How do boats help people?
qa.a: They carry people and goods across water
qa.e: Boats travel on rivers, lakes and seas, carrying people and goods.

qa.q: Reena drinks 6 glasses of water every day. How many glasses does she drink in 2 days?
qa.e: 6 glasses each day for 2 days is 6 + 6 = 12 glasses.

qa.q: Why should we keep our drinking water covered?
qa.a: To keep dust, flies and germs out
qa.e: Uncovered water can collect dust and germs from flies.

qa.q: Which habit saves water?
qa.a: Turning off the tap while brushing
qa.e: Turning the tap off when you are not using it stops water from going down the drain.

qa.q: What is rainwater harvesting?
qa.a: Collecting and storing rainwater for later use
qa.e: Rainwater from roofs can be collected in tanks or sent into the ground to refill groundwater.

qa.q: A tap leaks and wastes 1 bucket of water every day. How many buckets are wasted in a week?
qa.e: A week has 7 days. 1 bucket each day for 7 days is 7 buckets.

qa.q: Why should we save fresh water?
qa.a: Fresh water is limited and everyone needs it
qa.e: Most water on Earth is salty. Fresh water is limited, so we must not waste it.

qa.q: How can water used for washing vegetables be reused?
qa.e: This water is fine for plants, but not for drinking or cooking.

qa.q: Which is a better way to bathe and save water?
qa.e: A bucket bath uses a fixed amount of water and avoids waste.

qa.q: World Water Day is celebrated on ___.
qa.e: World Water Day is on 22 March. 5 June is World Environment Day.

qa.q: You see a tap running in the school washroom with no one using it. What should you do?
qa.a: Turn it off and tell a teacher if it is broken
qa.e: Turning off a running tap saves water. A broken tap should be reported so it can be fixed.

qa.q: Which of these do we get from animals?
qa.e: Milk comes from animals like cows, buffaloes and goats.

qa.q: Honey is made by which creature?
qa.e: Bees make honey from the nectar of flowers.

qa.q: Which of these is a millet?
qa.e: Ragi is a millet. Jowar and bajra are millets too.

qa.q: Rice and wheat are ___.
qa.e: Rice and wheat are cereal grains that give us energy.

qa.q: Which of these is a pulse?
qa.e: Pulses are dals like chana, moong, masoor and arhar.

qa.q: The year 2023 was celebrated as the International Year of ___.
qa.e: 2023 was the International Year of Millets, to make people aware of these healthy grains.

qa.q: Curd is made from ___.
qa.e: When a little curd is added to warm milk and left for some hours, the milk sets into curd.

qa.q: Which food comes from a plant?
qa.e: Peanuts are seeds of the groundnut plant, which grow under the soil.

qa.q: How are puris cooked?
qa.e: Puris puff up when fried in hot oil.

qa.q: How is dhokla cooked?
qa.e: Dhokla batter is cooked in steam, which makes it soft and spongy.

qa.q: Which food is cooked by boiling?
qa.e: Rice is cooked in boiling water until it is soft.

qa.q: Which of these can be eaten raw?
qa.e: Washed cucumbers are eaten raw in salads. Rajma, rice and flour must be cooked.

qa.q: Bread and cake are cooked in an oven. What is this method called?
qa.e: Cooking in the dry heat of an oven is called baking.

qa.q: Why should children not use the stove on their own?
qa.a: Fire and hot oil can cause burns
qa.e: Fire, hot pans and hot oil can burn us. Cooking must be done by or with an adult.

qa.q: Why do we wash fruits before eating them raw?
qa.e: Washing removes dust, dirt and germs from the skin of fruits.

qa.q: Bhutta (corn) is often cooked over hot coals. What is this method?
qa.e: Cooking food directly over a flame or hot coals is roasting.

qa.q: Dhokla is a famous dish from which state?
qa.e: Dhokla is a steamed snack from Gujarat.

qa.q: Which dish is popular in Punjab?
qa.a: Makki di roti and sarson da saag
qa.e: Makki di roti (maize roti) with sarson da saag (mustard greens) is a winter favourite in Punjab.

qa.q: Litti chokha is a famous dish of which state?
qa.e: Litti chokha is a well-known dish of Bihar.

qa.q: Why do people in different places eat different foods?
qa.a: Different crops grow in different places, and customs differ
qa.e: People cook with what grows near them, like rice in wet areas and coconut on coasts.

qa.q: People living near the sea often eat a lot of ___.
qa.e: Fish is easy to get near the sea, so it is common in coastal food.

qa.q: Idli and dosa are made from a batter of rice and ___.
qa.e: Idli and dosa batter is made by grinding soaked rice and urad dal.

qa.q: Dal baati churma is a famous dish from which state?
qa.e: Dal baati churma comes from Rajasthan.

qa.q: Puttu, a steamed rice dish, is popular in which state?
qa.e: Puttu, often eaten with kadala curry, is a favourite breakfast in Kerala.

qa.q: When should you wash your hands with soap?
qa.a: Before eating and after using the toilet
qa.e: Washing hands at these times stops germs from getting into our body.

qa.q: How many times a day should we brush our teeth?
qa.e: Brush twice a day: in the morning and before bed.

qa.q: Why should we keep our nails short and clean?
qa.a: Dirt and germs collect under long nails
qa.e: Germs under nails can go into our mouth with food.

qa.q: What should you do when you sneeze?
qa.a: Cover your nose and mouth with a tissue or your elbow
qa.e: Covering a sneeze stops germs from flying out and reaching others.

qa.q: What does hygiene mean?
qa.a: Keeping ourselves and our surroundings clean
qa.e: Hygiene is the habit of keeping clean to stay healthy.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT a clean habit?
qa.a: Eating food that has fallen on a dirty floor
qa.e: Food from a dirty floor can have germs. The others keep us clean.

qa.q: For about how long should you rub your hands with soap?
qa.e: Rubbing for about 20 seconds — humming 'Happy Birthday' twice — helps remove germs.

qa.q: Why should we keep our homes and surroundings clean?
qa.a: Dirt and stagnant water can breed flies and mosquitoes that spread illness
qa.e: Mosquitoes breed in standing water and flies sit on garbage. Both can spread illness.

qa.q: Why is exercise good for us?
qa.a: It makes our muscles, bones and heart strong
qa.e: Exercise keeps the body strong, fit and healthy.

qa.q: About how many hours of sleep do children of your age need each night?
qa.e: Children aged 6 to 12 need about 9 to 12 hours of sleep each night.

qa.q: On which date is International Day of Yoga celebrated?
qa.e: International Day of Yoga is celebrated every year on 21 June.

qa.q: Which of these is a good exercise?
qa.e: Skipping makes the heart beat faster and the legs strong.

qa.q: How long should children be active every day?
qa.e: Children should play or exercise for at least an hour every day.

qa.q: What can happen if you spend too long looking at a phone screen?
qa.e: Looking at screens for a long time can strain the eyes. Take breaks and play outside.

qa.q: Which is a traditional Indian outdoor game?
qa.e: Kho-kho is a chasing game played across India.

qa.q: Why do we need to rest after playing?
qa.a: Rest helps the body get back its energy
qa.e: When we rest and sleep, our body recovers and grows.

qa.q: What is a balanced meal?
qa.a: A meal with the right mix of different kinds of food
qa.e: A balanced meal has energy-giving, body-building and protective foods, plus water.

qa.q: Which of these is a body-building food?
qa.e: Dal is rich in protein, which helps our body grow and repair itself.

qa.q: Which of these is an energy-giving food?
qa.e: Roti, rice and potatoes give us energy to work and play.

qa.q: Why should we eat fruits and vegetables?
qa.a: They help protect us and keep us healthy
qa.e: Fruits and vegetables are protective foods that help the body stay healthy.

qa.q: Which lunch box is the most balanced?
qa.a: Roti, dal, sabzi and a fruit
qa.e: It has energy food (roti), body-building food (dal) and protective food (sabzi and fruit).

qa.q: How often should we eat junk food like chips and cold drinks?
qa.e: Junk food has too much salt, sugar or oil. It is fine only now and then.

qa.q: What is the best drink when you are thirsty?
qa.e: Clean water is the healthiest way to stop thirst.

qa.q: Raju eats 2 fruits every day. How many fruits does he eat in 5 days?
qa.e: 2 fruits each day for 5 days is 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10 fruits.

qa.q: Which of these is a natural thing?
qa.e: Trees grow in nature on their own. The others are made by people.

qa.q: Which of these is human-made?
qa.e: A bicycle is made by people in a factory. Rivers, the moon and mountains are natural.

qa.q: Paper is made from ___.
qa.e: Paper is made from wood pulp, which comes from trees. Old paper can also be recycled into new paper.

qa.q: Glass is made mainly from ___.
qa.e: Sand is heated to a very high temperature to make glass.

qa.q: Silk comes from ___.
qa.e: Silkworms spin cocoons of silk thread. The thread is used to weave silk cloth.

qa.q: Wool for sweaters comes from ___.
qa.e: Sheep have thick hair called wool, which is cut and spun into yarn.

qa.q: A tree is natural. What about a wooden table made from it?
qa.e: The table is human-made because a carpenter made it, even though wood is natural.

qa.q: Which of these is made from a plant?
qa.e: Cotton comes from the cotton plant. Wool and silk come from animals, and iron from rocks.

qa.q: What is a material?
qa.a: The stuff a thing is made of
qa.e: Wood, metal, plastic and glass are examples of materials.

qa.q: Which material are car tyres made of?
qa.e: Rubber is strong and bends without breaking, so it is used for tyres.

qa.q: Why do cooking pans often have plastic or wooden handles?
qa.a: They do not get hot quickly, so we can hold them
qa.e: Plastic and wood do not let heat pass through easily, so the handle stays cool.

qa.q: Which of these is a metal?
qa.e: Iron is a metal. Steel, copper and aluminium are metals too.

qa.q: A pencil is made of which two materials?
qa.e: The outside of a pencil is wood. The dark writing part inside is graphite.

qa.q: Which of these can be made of clay?
qa.e: Diyas and matkas are made by potters from clay.

qa.q: Rohan needs a bag to carry heavy books. Which material is best?
qa.e: Strong cloth does not tear easily and can hold heavy books.

qa.q: Why are windows made of glass?
qa.a: We can see through glass and light comes in
qa.e: Glass is see-through, so light comes in and we can look outside.

qa.q: Which material is see-through?
qa.e: We can see through clear glass. Wood, iron and cardboard block the view.

qa.q: Which of these soaks up water?
qa.e: A sponge has tiny holes that soak up water.

qa.q: Why are raincoats made of plastic?
qa.e: Plastic does not let water pass through, so we stay dry.

qa.q: Which of these will sink in water?
qa.e: A coin is small but heavy for its size, so it sinks. The others float.

qa.q: Which of these stretches and goes back to its shape?
qa.e: Rubber can stretch and return to its shape.

qa.q: Which of these breaks easily if dropped?
qa.e: Glass is hard but breaks easily when it hits the floor.

qa.q: Which of these is soft?
qa.e: Cotton is soft and fluffy. Stone, iron and brick are hard.

qa.q: Riya tested 7 things in water. 3 floated. How many sank?
qa.e: 7 things in all, 3 floated, so 7 − 3 = 4 sank.

qa.q: Who is an artisan?
qa.a: A skilled person who makes things by hand
qa.e: Potters, weavers, carpenters and basket makers are artisans.

qa.q: What does a weaver use to make cloth?
qa.e: A weaver passes threads over and under each other on a loom to make cloth.

qa.q: Who makes tools from iron by heating and beating it?
qa.e: A blacksmith heats iron until it glows and then shapes it with a hammer.

qa.q: In Hindi, what is the potter's spinning wheel called?
qa.e: The potter's wheel is called a chaak. A charkha is a spinning wheel for making thread.

qa.q: Why does a potter bake clay pots in a kiln?
qa.a: To make them hard and strong
qa.e: The great heat of the kiln makes clay hard, so the pot can hold water.

qa.q: A carpenter mainly works with ___.
qa.e: Carpenters make doors, tables and chairs from wood.

qa.q: Which of these is made by a basket maker?
qa.e: Basket makers weave baskets from bamboo, cane or grass.

qa.q: A potter makes 5 diyas every hour. How many diyas will he make in 4 hours?
qa.e: 5 diyas each hour for 4 hours is 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 diyas.

qa.q: Madhubani painting comes from which state?
qa.e: Madhubani painting is a famous art of the Mithila region of Bihar.

qa.q: Which painting style uses simple white shapes like circles and triangles?
qa.e: Warli paintings from Maharashtra use simple white shapes on a dark background.

qa.q: Channapatna in Karnataka is famous for ___.
qa.e: Channapatna makes smooth, brightly coloured wooden toys.

qa.q: Blue pottery is a famous craft of which city?
qa.e: Jaipur in Rajasthan is known for its blue pottery.

qa.q: Pashmina shawls come from ___.
qa.e: Soft, warm pashmina shawls come from Kashmir.

qa.q: How is bandhani cloth made?
qa.a: By tying small parts of cloth and dyeing it
qa.e: Small bits of cloth are tied tightly with thread before dyeing, so those parts stay uncoloured.

qa.q: Pattachitra is a painting style from which state?
qa.e: Pattachitra paintings on cloth are a famous art of Odisha.

qa.q: Which material is used for many crafts in Assam and the North-East?
qa.e: Bamboo grows well in the North-East, so many baskets and crafts are made from bamboo and cane.

qa.q: What can you make from an empty plastic bottle?
qa.e: A cut plastic bottle can hold soil and a small plant.

qa.q: Which useful thing can be made from old newspapers?
qa.e: Newspapers can be folded and glued into strong paper bags.

qa.q: Why should we make useful things from waste?
qa.a: It reduces garbage and saves materials
qa.e: Using waste again means less garbage and fewer new things need to be made.

qa.q: What should you do before cutting a tin or a bottle for a craft?
qa.e: Cut edges can be sharp. An adult can cut safely or help you.

qa.q: Old clothes can be cut into strips and woven into a ___.
qa.e: Cloth strips can be braided or woven into a soft doormat.

qa.q: Why should you wash an old jar before turning it into a pen stand?
qa.a: To remove leftover food and germs
qa.e: Leftover food can smell and attract ants and germs.

qa.q: Which of these should NOT be used for a craft at home?
qa.e: Broken glass is sharp and can cut your hands.

qa.q: Pinki made 3 pen stands from old tins, and Bunty made 4. How many pen stands did they make together?
qa.e: 3 + 4 = 7 pen stands.

qa.q: Which of these is wet waste?
qa.e: Vegetable peels come from plants and rot easily, so they are wet waste.

qa.q: Which of these is dry waste?
qa.e: Paper is dry waste. The others are food waste, which is wet waste.

qa.q: What happens to a banana peel left in the soil for some weeks?
qa.a: It rots and mixes with the soil
qa.e: Tiny living things in the soil break down the peel.

qa.q: Why is plastic harmful when thrown on the ground?
qa.a: It does not rot and can harm animals
qa.e: Plastic stays for a very long time. Animals can eat it by mistake and get sick.

qa.q: Which of these should be handed over carefully by an adult and not mixed with other waste?
qa.e: Batteries have harmful things inside, so they need special care.

qa.q: Why should we not burn garbage?
qa.a: The smoke dirties the air and is bad for our health
qa.e: Burning garbage, especially plastic, gives off harmful smoke.

qa.q: What is waste?
qa.a: Things we throw away because we do not need them
qa.e: Waste is anything we throw away after use.

qa.q: Riya's family throws away 5 bags of wet waste and 3 bags of dry waste in a week. How many more bags of wet waste than dry waste is that?
qa.e: 5 − 3 = 2 more bags of wet waste.

qa.q: In many Indian cities, which colour bin is used for wet waste?
qa.e: Green bins are for wet waste and blue bins are for dry waste.

qa.q: What is compost?
qa.a: A rich manure made from rotted wet waste
qa.e: Compost is made when wet waste rots. It makes soil rich for plants.

qa.q: Which of these can go into a compost pit?
qa.e: Vegetable peels rot and become compost. Plastic, glass and metal do not.

qa.q: Which living things help turn wet waste into compost?
qa.e: Earthworms and tiny living things in the soil break down wet waste.

qa.q: Why should we sort waste into wet and dry?
qa.a: So wet waste becomes compost and dry waste can be recycled
qa.e: Sorting makes it possible to compost and recycle waste.

qa.q: Which colour bin is used for dry waste in many Indian cities?
qa.e: The blue bin is for dry waste like paper, plastic, glass and metal.

qa.q: How is compost useful?
qa.a: It makes the soil rich so plants grow well
qa.e: Compost adds goodness to the soil, like manure.

qa.q: An empty milk packet should go into which bin?
qa.e: A milk packet is plastic. Rinse it and put it with dry waste.

qa.q: What does 'reduce' mean?
qa.a: Use fewer things so less waste is made
qa.e: Reducing means making less waste in the first place.

qa.q: Using an old jam jar to store pencils is an example of ___.
qa.e: The jar is used again for a new job, so it is reused.

qa.q: Old newspapers are made into new paper at a factory. This is ___.
qa.e: Turning old paper into new paper is recycling.

qa.q: Which habit helps reduce plastic waste?
qa.a: Carrying a cloth bag for shopping
qa.e: A cloth bag can be used many times, so fewer plastic bags are needed.

qa.q: Who buys old newspapers, bottles and metal from homes so they can be recycled?
qa.e: The kabadiwala collects these things and sends them to be recycled.

qa.q: Giving your old storybooks to a younger cousin is an example of ___.
qa.e: The books are used again by someone else, so they are reused.

qa.q: Which of these can be recycled?
qa.e: Glass can be melted and made into new glass. The others are wet waste for compost.

qa.q: A family used to bring home 10 plastic bags a week. Now they bring only 4. By how many bags have they reduced their waste?
qa.e: 10 − 4 = 6 fewer plastic bags each week.
